findings.problem: The video ends on a frame caught mid-loop. The three recap rows loop independently, and the last frame (t=8.99) shows row 1 tiles squashed at different widths, row 3 letters E/G/J/A piled on top of each other, and the tick badge faded to an almost invisible ghost. The held end frame (and any poster taken from it) looks broken.
findings.fix: Make every row loop settle on its clean final pose before the scene ends (for example freeze each row at its end state from about t=6.5 s, or choose loop periods that divide the scene length). Row 3 should finish on the green valid-tour pose with the tick drawn. Row 1 should finish on a tidy row of five tiles.
findings.evidence: Stills s11@8.99 (messy), s11@8.8 (tick half-drawn), s11@4 and s11@6 (clean). Source: loop() in scene-11-recap.js.

findings.problem: Colour roles break within the video. The tournament winner gets a BLUE tick, while every other scene uses green for correct or valid (scene 3 tick, valid-tour badge in scene 8, recap). The red cross and blue tick also sit over the corner of the tiles, partly covering the '3' and '5' tiles.
findings.fix: Use the green tick for the winner and keep blue for the parent tag only (the rule is green = correct or valid, blue = the main subject). Nudge the tick and cross so they sit above the tile corner instead of overlapping the numeral.
findings.evidence: Still s7@5: blue tick over tile 5, red cross over tile 3. Compare s3@5, where the tick is green.

findings.problem: Purple has no single role. In scenes 2 and 3 purple means the new child (0.5, 0.7), while in scene 9 it means parent 2 and the children there are grey. The same colour therefore stands for 'offspring' in one scene and 'second parent' in another. The orange tag 'not drawn' in scene 7 is also an odd use of orange, which is meant for attention or chosen.
findings.fix: Pick one role. Either keep purple for the second parent and operator only, and make new children blue (the thing changed) in scenes 2 and 3, or make children purple in scene 9 too. Make 'not drawn' grey or red-tinted.
findings.evidence: Stills s2@12.8 and s3@5 (purple children), s9@6 (purple parent 2, grey child labels), s7@5 (orange 'not drawn').

findings.problem: The heat-map cards have no legend. Orange cells, light green cells and dark green cells are never named, so a first-timer must guess that orange means 'copies of the best' and green shades mean other fitness values. The orange pill ('12 / 12') is not tied to the cells either.
findings.fix: Add one small key at the bottom (an orange swatch labelled 'best copies') or colour-match the count pill ('12 / 12') to the cell colour with a short label.

findings.problem: Around t=4 to 5.5 the rank column fills in while the chance bars still show the old roulette values (99%, 98%, 0.4%). For about a second 'rank 5' sits beside 98% before the bars rebuild to 33%.
findings.fix: Hide or fade the old bars when the rank column starts to appear, or move them to the new values at the same time.
findings.evidence: Stills s6@4 and s6@5 (98% beside rank 5), against s6@6 (34%).

findings.problem: The page title reads 'Lecture 4 · Lecture 4: Selection, operators and encodings', so 'Lecture 4' is repeated. Lectures 5 and 6 use 'Lecture N · Topic'.
findings.fix: Set the title to 'Lecture 4 · Selection and operators · CSLingo video', matching the other pages.
findings.evidence: videos/lecture-4.html line 6, against lecture-5.html and lecture-6.html.

findings.problem: The recap leaves about 90 px of empty stage under the rows, and the 'Beat the Lecture 4 boss quiz' button appears only late. Rows 1 and 3 are small pictograms and carry little of the lecture (nothing for crossover or tournament).
findings.fix: Optional: add a fourth row for the selection methods, or space the rows out to use the stage.
